chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Musa ibn al-Qasim al-Bajali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, who said:

Muhammad ibn Isma'il came to me while we had performed the Rajab 'umrah and were then in Makkah. He said, "O uncle, I intend to go to Baghdad, and I wished to bid farewell to my uncle Abu al-Hasan"—meaning Musa ibn Ja'far عليه السلام—"and I wished that you would go with me to him."

So I went out with him toward my brother, and he was in his house in al-Hawbah, shortly after al-Maghrib. I knocked at the door, and my brother answered me, saying, "Who is this?" I said, "Ali." He said, "I am just coming out." He was slow in wudu (ablution), so I said, "Quickly!" He said, "I am hurrying." Then he came out, wearing a striped waist-wrapper tied at his neck, until he sat beneath the threshold of the door.

Ali ibn Ja'far said: I bent toward him and kissed his head, and said, "I have come to you concerning a matter: if you see it as right, may Allah grant him success in it; and if it is otherwise than that, how often we err." He said, "What is it?" I said, "This son of your brother wishes to bid you farewell and depart for Baghdad." He said to me, "Call him." So I called him, and he had stood aside. He came near him, kissed his head, and said, "May I be your ransom, advise me."

He said, "I advise you to be Godwary regarding my blood." He replied to him, "Whoever intends evil toward you, may Allah deal with him accordingly," and he began supplicating against whoever intended evil toward him. Then he returned, kissed his head, and said, "O uncle, advise me." He said, "I advise you to be Godwary regarding my blood." He said, "Whoever intends evil toward you, may Allah deal with him accordingly," and he did so. Then he returned, kissed his head, and again said, "O uncle, advise me." He said, "I advise you to be Godwary regarding my blood." So he supplicated against whoever intended evil toward him, then withdrew from him, and I left with him.

Then my brother said to me, "O Ali, stay where you are." So I remained in my place. He entered his house, then called me, and I entered to him. He took a purse containing one hundred dinars, gave it to me, and said, "Tell your nephew to use it for assistance on his journey."

Ali said: I took it and tucked it into the edge of my cloak. Then he handed me another hundred and said, "Give him this as well." Then he handed me another purse and said, "Give him this as well." I said, "May I be your ransom, if you fear from him what you mentioned, then why do you aid him against yourself?" He said, "If I maintain ties with him and he cuts me off, Allah will cut off his term." Then he took a leather cushion containing three thousand bright dirhams and said, "Give him this as well."

He said: I went out to him and gave him the first hundred, and he rejoiced in it greatly and prayed for his uncle. Then I gave him the second and the third, and he rejoiced in them until I thought he would turn back and not depart. Then I gave him the three thousand dirhams. So he continued on his way until he entered upon Harun, greeted him as caliph, and said, "I did not think that there were two caliphs on the earth until I saw my uncle Musa ibn Ja'far being greeted as caliph." Harun then sent him one hundred thousand dirhams, but Allah struck him with angina, and he did not look at even a dirham of it, nor touch it.

key_terms.أُوصِيكَ: I advise you; a solemn form of counsel or instruction
key_terms.الْخِلَافَةِ: the caliphate; political rule or leadership
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual washing before acts of worship
key_terms.تَتَّقِيَ اللَّهَ: to have taqwa toward Allah; to be Godwary and avoid wrongdoing
key_terms.دِينَارٍ: a gold coin used as currency
key_terms.صُرَّةً: a purse or bag containing money
key_terms.عُمْرَةَ رَجَبٍ: the minor pilgrimage performed in the month of Rajab
key_terms.فِي دَمِي: with respect to my blood; meaning concerning causing or facilitating his killing

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith of Muhammad ibn Isma'il’s visit to Imam Musa ibn Ja'far عليه السلام say about kinship, betrayal, and the Imam’s foreknowledge?
ai.summary: This report narrates Muhammad ibn Isma'il’s farewell visit to Imam Musa ibn Ja'far عليه السلام before departing to Baghdad, along with the Imam’s repeated warning: "Fear Allah regarding my blood." It also recounts the Imam’s generosity toward a relative despite foreknowledge of harm, and the eventual betrayal before Harun, followed by the betrayer’s sudden death before benefiting from the reward he received.
